study.title: Immediate Analgesic Effect of Acupuncture in Patients With Primary Dysmenorrhea: A fMRI Study
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial with task-state and resting-state fMRI
study.blinding: Patients, assessors, and statisticians blinded to groupings
study.population: Right-handed nulliparous women aged 18-30 years with primary dysmenorrhea
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) right-handed nulliparous women aged 18–30 years; (2) meeting the diagnostic criteria for PDM of the Society of Obstetricians and Gynecologists of Canada (Burnett and Lemyre, 2017); (3) normal menstrual cycle (27 to 32 days); (4) fulfillment of a menstrual cycle dysmenorrhea diary; (5) average pain intensity score of ≥4 on a visual analog scale (VAS) for three consecutive menstrual cycles; (6) fMRI scan performed on days 1–3 of menstruation and a VAS pain score of ≥ 4 before the scan; and (7) responsive to acupuncture and able to attain the feeling of De qi
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) dysmenorrhea caused by organic gynecological disease; (2) history of cardiovascular and/or cerebrovascular diseases and/or neuropsychiatric disorders; (3) intake of painkillers or sedatives within 1 week before the fMRI scan; (4) contraindications to fMRI

extraction_notes.note: Trial registration number is not reported anywhere in the paper.

Number of patients assigned to each arm before dropout is not reported. Only completion numbers are given (19 RA, 15 SA; total 34 completers from 44 enrolled with 9 dropouts; arithmetic implies 44-9=35 expected but paper states 34, suggesting one further issue or reporting discrepancy not resolved in the text).
44 enrolled - 9 dropouts = 35, but 34 completers are reported. The paper states '9 patients dropped out' and '34 patients...completed.' This 1-patient discrepancy is not explained in the paper.

Deqi sensation was an inclusion criterion (patients must be able to attain De qi), but no quantitative deqi measurement instrument or scores (e.g., MASS subscales) were reported. Sensory responses during acupuncture were not quantitatively assessed.
Expectancy/credibility of treatment was not formally measured or reported. The paper does not mention any expectancy or treatment credibility scale.

The coordinate space is labeled 'MNI coordinates (RAI)' in Table 2. RAI typically refers to Right-Anterior-Inferior orientation convention, which differs from the standard LPI (Left-Posterior-Inferior) convention used by most MNI-based software. This may affect interpretation of the x-coordinate signs. Extracted coordinates are reported exactly as in the table without conversion.

Coordinates for the rACC-left precentral gyrus functional connectivity result are only presented as a brain image in Figure 4A. No coordinate table was provided for the FC result. Coordinates were not extracted for this result.
Supplementary Figure 1 (flow chart of fMRI study) is referenced but not included in the provided PDF. Details about participant flow through the imaging study may be in this supplement.

The task-state fMRI analysis used a block design paradigm, but the exact statistical model for the task-state analysis (e.g., HRF convolution details, number of regressors) is not fully described beyond 'one-sample t test,' 'paired t test,' and '2 × 2 ANOVA.'
The TR for T1-weighted images is listed as 'TR = 2530 mm' in the paper, which appears to be a typographical error (should likely be 2530 ms). Extracted exactly as reported.
Flip angle, number of slices, and other acquisition parameters for the resting-state EPI sequence are not fully reported beyond TR, TE, FOV, flip angle (90°), slice thickness, and resolution.

The laterality of sham acupuncture stimulation (bilateral vs. unilateral) is not explicitly stated; the real acupuncture was bilateral SP6, but for sham the text does not specify 'bilateral' explicitly.

The cluster size for the rACC in the Twirling/Retention vs. RA/SA contrast row is listed as '62*' with asterisk indicating small volume correction, while R.SMA(6) has voxel size 246 without asterisk, suggesting different correction methods were applied to these two regions within the same contrast.
No between-group comparison of post-treatment VAS scores reached statistical significance (p = 0.069). The primary clinical outcome showing group difference was VAS(B-A) and VAS(B-A)/A.

Resting-state fMRI functional connectivity thresholding and correction methods for the group comparison of FC change are not reported in detail. Only the final result (significant group difference in rACC–left precentral gyrus FC) is described.
Imaging data during the non-menstrual period were not collected due to financial constraints, as acknowledged in the limitations section.
